children: Tyson Foods, Inc.
stock rose Monday after the meat producer reported better-than-expected fourth-quarter earnings and revenue and raised
During Monday’s earnings call, CEO
Jeffrey Schomburger
called protein the “biggest opportunity in food,” citing a $273 billion retail category growing faster than the broader food market.
He noted that seven in 10 Americans are trying to eat more protein, while younger households spend more than three times as much on protein each week as their parents.
Tyson is targeting younger consumers with more protein-rich products, bolder flavors and simpler ingredients.
Adjusted earnings fell 47% year over year to 61 cents per share, beating the analyst
Sales increased 5.2% year over year to $14.585 billion, exceeding the consensus estimate of $14.169 billion.
Excluding an additional week and legal contingency accruals, sales declined 4%.

GAAP operating income fell $157 million to $1 million, while adjusted operating income declined 41% to $361 million. Tyson swung to a GAAP loss of 22 cents per share from earnings of 13 cents a year earlier.
Tyson generated $2.4 billion in operating cash flow and $1.7 billion in free cash flow during fiscal 2026. Capital expenditures totaled $770 million.
Segment Performance
Prepared Foods sales rose 0.4% to $2.6 billion, while operating income increased $43 million to $321 million.
Chicken sales grew 1.3% to $4.5 billion, supported by 2% volume growth. Operating income reached $389 million.
Beef sales fell 10.5% to $4.9 billion as tight cattle supplies reduced volumes by 12.7%. The segment’s operating loss widened to $171 million from $52 million.
Pork sales increased 2.4% to $1.4 billion, while international sales rose 6.1% to $619 million.
Beef Restructuring and Dividend Increase
Tyson is reorganizing its beef operations around three central U.S. facilities to improve efficiency. It plans to fully restore the second shift at its Amarillo, Texas, plant by summer 2027.
The company also plans a long-term partnership with
Allied Beef Co.
to strengthen domestic cattle supplies.
Tyson returned $1.1 billion to shareholders during fiscal 2026 through dividends and share repurchases.
Tyson also disclosed Monday that its board had raised the quarterly Class A dividend to 52 cents per share on Friday, marking its 15th consecutive year of annual dividend increases.
Fiscal 2027 Outlook
Tyson expects fiscal 2027 sales of $53.316 billion to $54.444 billion, below the analyst
The company expects adjusted sales to decline 3.5% to 5.5%, reflecting lower beef volumes and tight cattle supplies.
Tyson forecasts adjusted operating income of $1.7 billion to $2.15 billion and free cash flow of $800 million to $1.3 billion.
TSN Price Action:
Tyson Foods shares were up 7.29% at $63.11 at the time of publication on Monday,
